bull_bear.body:
- Cane pest/disease infestation concentrated in dominant cane varieties — Top Borer, Early Shoot Borer and Red Rot infestations observed over the last three-four years mainly impact the CO-238 & CO-118 cane varieties, which occupy the major portion of the Company's cane area; mitigation relies on integrated pest management and phasing out CO-238 over coming years.
- Shrinking cane-growing land in the command area — Rapid urbanisation and industrial expansion in Western Uttar Pradesh is reducing the cultivable agricultural land available for cane cultivation, a structural threat to feedstock availability.
- Government policy dependence for sugar realisations — The Company's expected sugar selling-price range for FY27 explicitly hinges on there being no revision in Minimum Support Price (MSP), ethanol-blending policy, or export policy - realisations are largely outside management's control.
- Global commodity-price and geopolitical exposure — World sugar prices are driven by crude oil (sugar/ethanol parity), the war in West Asian countries, and the global sugar demand-supply balance, exposing the Company's export/parity economics to factors outside its control.
- Profitability compression — Per the SEBI (LODR) significant-changes disclosure, Operating Profit Margin fell from 6.88% to 4.91% and Net Profit Margin from 4.94% to 2.35% year-on-year, while Return on Net Worth dropped from 15.19% to 7.00%, indicating margin and earnings pressure during the year.
- Legislative risk on employee benefit obligations — The government may amend the Code of Social Security, 2020, requiring higher gratuity/benefit payments to employees, which would directly increase the present value of the Company's defined benefit obligation.

business.body: Mawana Sugars Limited manufactures sugar and generates power at two complexes in Uttar Pradesh (Mawana Sugars Works and Nanglamal Sugar Complex), and produces industrial alcohol (ethanol) at its Nanglamal Distillery. Sugar is sold in the domestic market while ethanol, produced from B-Heavy and C-Heavy molasses, is supplied to Oil Marketing Companies under the government's ethanol-blending programme.

outlook.body:
- Replacing the CO-238 cane variety and applying integrated pest-management techniques over the coming years to reduce Top Borer/Red Rot impact on cane yield.
- Structured HR transformation to align with the new Labour Codes, strengthen governance, and enhance employee experience.
- Continued investment in capability building and leadership development, including the 'UDAAN' Assessment and Development Center initiative, to strengthen the internal leadership pipeline.
- Talent acquisition, training and diversity & inclusion initiatives treated as an ongoing strategic priority.
- Digitisation of HR processes via SAP Success Factors ('Project Pragati') to standardise processes and enable data-driven performance management.
- Continuing to upgrade internal control systems on an ongoing basis, supported by SAP and other software systems.

Separately, under technology absorption, a rotary sugar dryer / sugar cooling & drying system of 20 MT capacity was installed (destination cut off in the source text).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- All-India sugar closing stock estimated at around 46 Lac Tons by 30 September 2026 - sufficient for just under two months of domestic consumption and the lowest inventory level in the past decade, a tight domestic supply backdrop.
- Company's sugar selling price is expected to stay in the same range in FY27 as FY26, unless government policy on MSP, ethanol blending, or exports changes.
- World sugar prices will continue to be driven by crude oil (sugar/ethanol parity), the war in West Asian countries, and the global sugar demand-supply balance.
- Ethanol blending is approaching the government's 20% target (19.98% achieved in tender year 2025-26), reinforced by the mandatory E20 petrol-blending policy from 1 April 2026 and BIS specifications for E22/E25/E27/E30, with the government drafting rules for even higher blends (E85-E100) - a structural tailwind for ethanol offtake.

open.item: Board recommended a final dividend of 40% (Rs 4.00 per equity share of Rs 10 each) for FY26, subject to shareholder approval at the ensuing AGM.
Company is allocated 38,000 KL of ethanol from B-Heavy & C-Heavy Molasses by Oil Marketing Companies for the Ethanol Supply Year 2025-26 (November 2025 to October 2026).

Sugar selling price is expected to remain in the same range as FY26 (Rs 4081-4151-4021) during April 2026 to March 2027, unless there is a revision in government MSP, ethanol-blending, or export policy.

Proposed amalgamation of wholly-owned subsidiary Mawana Foods Private Limited (MFPL) with the Company; Scheme of Amalgamation approved by shareholders and unsecured creditors and filed before the NCLT, with NCLT approval awaited.

Company to purchase a commercial property in institutional sector-32, Gurugram, from a related party for total consideration of Rs 28 crore, to establish its Corporate Office; legal/regulatory transfer formalities are under process.

Management is replacing the CO-238 cane variety and applying integrated pest-management techniques in coming years to minimize the impact of Top Borer, Early Shoot Borer and Red Rot in the Company's command area.
Rapid urbanisation and industrial expansion in Western Uttar Pradesh is reducing cultivable agricultural land available for cane cultivation.

Scheme of amalgamation between wholly-owned subsidiary Mawana Foods Private Limited and the Company, duly approved by shareholders and unsecured creditors, has been filed before the NCLT; approval is awaited.
